decisions.choice: Stock list is a vertical Ultima Toggle Group with one pressed item; the pressed row's background is overridden to --ult-color-accent-subtle
decisions.why: Single selection with keyboard support from a kit component, matching a shipped block. The kit's raised-surface pressed state was nearly invisible, so the brand accent marks the selection.

decisions.choice: Log-a-donation form is inline in a Card, with Category as a portalled Ultima Select
decisions.why: Volunteers log donations constantly at the intake desk; keeping the form on screen avoids an extra step. The Select provides keyboard open, Escape close and focus return.

decisions.choice: A donation whose name matches an existing item (case-insensitive) adds to its quantity, keeps its existing category and sets its last-restocked date to today; any other name adds a new item. The affected item becomes the selected item.
decisions.why: The brief says the form 'adds to an existing one'; matching on name is what a volunteer expects, and showing the result in the detail confirms the change.

decisions.choice: Quantity defaults to 1 and must be a whole number of at least 1, with its own field error
decisions.why: Prevents zero, negative or fractional counts from corrupting stock.

decisions.choice: Items at or below 5 on hand show a warning-tone 'Low stock' badge; category badges use the neutral tone
decisions.why: A status the pantry needs, expressed with the warning role as the brief requires. The category stays neutral so neither accent nor status color carries category meaning.

decisions.choice: Brand accent appears on the 'Larder' wordmark (--ult-color-accent-text), the primary 'Log donation' button (Button's default accent tone) and the selected row
options: Accent on wordmark, primary action and selection
decisions.why: Uses the berry magenta as the product's accent without giving it any status meaning.

decisions.choice: The 48rem breakpoint lives in the app token module (src/components/pantry/screen.stylex.ts) as `stylex.defineConsts`, beside the app size tokens --app-size-content-max (72rem, as in the Projects lesson) and --app-size-page-min (100dvh)
options: defineConsts in the app token module
Named module constant in pantry.tsx, as Ultima's principles and the Projects lesson do
decisions.why: The brief allows lengths only in theme and token modules; StyleX compiles an imported defineConsts media query (verified in the production CSS as `@media (width >= 48rem)`).

decisions.choice: Laptop layout: stock list in the left column spanning two rows; item detail and donation form stacked in the right column. Phone order: list, detail, form.
options: List left, detail and form right
decisions.why: Keeps list and detail side by side as required, without the form crowding either.

decisions.choice: Did not load the Figtree or IBM Plex Mono faces named by the theme; the system fallback stack renders
decisions.why: The docs allow either; loading them would need font files the public host does not provide, from another source.

decisions.choice: Kept the documented `import '../ultima-theme.css'` after index.css in src/main.tsx, even though the production stylesheet emits the unlayered theme before StyleX's `@layer priority*` blocks
options: Keep the documented import and verify computed values
Restructure the build to emit the theme last
decisions.why: The unlayered theme beats layered StyleX variables regardless of file order. Computed --ult-color-accent on the root, a Button and the portalled Select popup matched the export in system dark (#e968be), system light (#bb2893), data-theme=dark and data-theme=light.

decisions.choice: Seed data: eight items across all four categories (two each), with restock dates in late September and early October 2026, two of them low stock
decisions.why: Exercises every category in the fixed set and the low-stock state.

decisions.choice: Scaffolded with npm and create-vite's react-ts template; kept the template's oxlint and ran ESLint after it (`oxlint && eslint .`)
decisions.why: npm is the package manager the docs' commands use; the lint script follows the Install page's advice for an app that already has oxlint.
